verdict: On fields where nothing changed, the satellite organic-matter estimate still jumps by about 0.14 points from one year to the next, while a good rotation is expected to add only 0.1 to 0.3 points in ten years, so on a single field real change is buried in noise. Averaging many fields does not fix this, because within one kind of soil the estimate cannot be shown to follow organic matter (it mostly tells sand from loam) and it shifts with whatever crop residue lies on the surface; compare rotations by bare days (how long the soil sits uncovered each year) instead, which measures how exposed the soil is, not what the soil has become.

notes.om_pred: om_pred is a rough picture of the kind of soil (sand against loam). Its year-to-year movement and its trend on a field are noise and crop residue, not soil change.
notes.bare_days: bare_days measures how long the soil sat uncovered, which is exposure, not what the soil has become. One field-year only tells a fallow year from a cropped year; compare rotations on multi-year means over many fields, within the same years.
notes.confidence: confidence says how repeatable om_pred is in that row (how often and how fully the field was seen bare, and whether the two satellites agreed), scaled by the model's overall skill. It is not accuracy: it does not tell a good year from a bad year of the same field, and on sandy soils higher confidence goes with a larger error.

model.label: organic_matter_pct of data/fields.parquet: SSURGO om_r, surface horizon, area-weighted over the field's map units
model.what_accuracy_means: SSURGO om_r is the soil survey's representative value for a mapped soil, not a measurement of the field. Accuracy here = how well bare-soil reflectance tells which mapped soil a field lies on, for a soil map unit the model has never seen. It says nothing about following organic matter that changes over time.

schemes_explained.map_unit: grouped by dominant soil map unit, model size chosen inside each training fold (HEADLINE)
schemes_explained.map_unit_fixed: grouped by dominant soil map unit, fixed model size (like-for-like with the rows below)
schemes_explained.series: grouped by soil series: map units of one series share a fold (stricter than the headline)
schemes_explained.field: grouped by field (leaks through the map unit)
schemes_explained.random: plain random K-fold over rows (leaks; the number that lies)

headline.what: om_pred of the table (both families combined), out-of-fold by dominant map unit

confidence.formula: confidence = skill x tau2 / (tau2 + v x g); see pipeline/soil/confidence.py
confidence.meaning: confidence says how repeatable om_pred is in that row (how often and how fully the field was seen bare, and whether the two satellites agreed), scaled by the model's overall skill. It is not accuracy: it does not tell a good year from a bad year of the same field, and on sandy soils higher confidence goes with a larger error.
